title: Sasquatch encounters on the back roads
excerpt: Back Roads Bill recounts presenting at North Bay Sasquatch conference
content:
There are many unexplained occurrences on the back roads. You know this.

Who gets to attend a Sasquatch conference, let alone present?

I did on both accounts.

Earlier on the Saturday of Thanksgiving weekend, there was a Sasquatch conference in North Bay. More than 150 interested people crammed into a small church hall for the day.

A cryptid is an animal or being whose existence is claimed by folklore and local sightings. There is the study of cryptozoology (the study of hidden or unknown animals), but it lacks scientific proof or recognition.

One of the most interesting questions posed at the conference was a spontaneous one from the crowd of Bigfoot enthusiasts who asked for a show of hands.

“For all of us…do you think Sasquatch is flesh and blood or connected to the paranormal?”

You can think about it.

(Read to the end for the results.)

I reported a Sasquatch encounter in the late summer of 2024 near Red Lake. Within the Sunset Country tourism region, it purports Sasquatch sightings. In and around Dryden-Vermilion Bay, there are several Sasquatch figurines roadside.

Conference

By observation and declaration, many First Nations people attended; some told their stories.

One was Ken Dokis, from Nipissing First Nation, a former police chief, who recalled his story to the conference attendees, which you can listen to on the Back Roads Bill podcast, Episode 33. For Ken, it was a deep, personal experience that he did not fully share until the podcast, two years back.

Ken explained Sabe (Sabé or Misabe) is believed to be closer to the spirit world than humans and reminds us that we must be truthful to who we are. The Ojibwa expression Kitchi-Sabe means to walk tall, or to have integrity. It is only by being honest that we can have integrity.

Elders will say, "Never try to be someone else; live true to your spirit, be honest to yourself, and accept who you are the way the Creator made you."

And there is the element of “shape shifting.” It was recalled that traditional stories say the Creator sent Sabe to walk among humans to remind them to be true to their word, avoid gossip, and live genuine lives. Sabe is chosen for honesty because he is massive but walks through the forest without pretense; he does not need to hide who or what he is.

Stories

Many participants recalled their encounters.

Jackie Lange now lives in Redbridge just to the east of North Bay (Highway 63 to Quebec).

Her story is featured in Dan Hammond’s book, From the Shadows – True Cryptid Encounters. The author was at the conference. He is also a podcast host, ‘Phantom Faction ’- a podcast to guide, inform, assist, and educate anyone interested in the paranormal.” He said, “This book brings together true, firsthand accounts of encounters with some of the world's most mysterious cryptids.”

Within his book, “In the winter of 1981-82, a 19-year-old woman and a coworker on a farm in Manitoba, Canada, experience a terrifying evening while tending to mares for the evening. What follows, which can only be labeled as dissociative amnesia, over the next 20+ years, is awakened by nature’s most mystical creatures - the hoot of an owl.”

Jackie was 19 years old. “I basically had no recollection of it since 1981-82 until that evening in 2017.

“It was the owl call that got my attention, and it did not echo between the houses. It triggered fear so intense I hid in the house below the height of the counters not to be seen. That started my journey to understand and hopefully to alleviate my fear.”

Why did she attend the gathering? “I sought out the conference for two reasons- one to share and confirm with a like-minded community that Sabe is a tangible, real being, and to also be accepted by the same community and seek understanding. I need no further proof of their existence; they should be respected.”

She said author Dan Hammond “put out feelers to everyone on Ontario Sasquatch for stories as he was putting a book together. I wrote out my story, and that was that. I was honored that it made it in his book when he introduced himself at the conference.”

“My story of understanding and seeking answers started when I heard the owl hoot when I moved to the North Shore of Lake Erie. I first sought Peter Smith (founder of Ontario Sasquatch), and he was helpful in asking me questions to further get the memory out and encouraged me to keep talking to people.”

She then reached out to Thom Cantrall from Washington State (sixty years of Sasquatch research): “He pointed me to other names and books that would have answers for me. I was terrified of shadows - unknown noises at night and built myself up with fake fear of the what if that sound was- or scenarios of what if I opened the door and a Bigfoot was standing there?”

She wished Back Roads Bill a wish. “I do hope you get your encounter - as I have heard many say- 'Expect the unexpected.'”

Then, spontaneously, within the audience, Jackie gifted an indigenous drum, a prized possession, signed by Bob Gimlin of the famous Sasquatch film clip.

“It was near the end of the conference; I left to retrieve the shipping box to pack the drum-on my return, Jenn was speaking, the woman who is making it law in her community (Adikamegoshii-ziibiing - Birch Island Whitefish River FN) to respect, bring no harm to known and unknown creatures. I was listening to her as I stood beside Peter Smith, and when she finished, I was overcome with the urge that the drum was intended for her now.”

“I said how my time with it is over and that it is not for sale, but would she like it as a gift to help her in her pursuit of lawmaking. She said she has been staring at it and has been dreaming about that painted face.

Post conference. “I woke up the next morning with a feeling like I did this before - it felt familiar and wonder if the drum was in fact always meant for her and I was just a vehicle to get it to her. I feel wonderful it is with her; she understands the potential and has already smudged with it.”

It was one of those unscripted moments that are unexplained.

Mind speak

Christine Byrnes has long been a believer. She was one of the keynote speakers. Her encounter is in an early BRB Sasquatch story and on the podcasts, episodes 38 and 39. She has also spoken with famed Sasquatch author John Bingernagel, a Ph.D. researcher. I interviewed him in this article on Jan. 26, 2022. He has passed since. As a Bingernagel cryptid plaster cast was passed around in the audience, many took photos. Peter Smith and Christine are both cited in the article and in the podcasts.

“I believe in the collective consciousness of Sasquatch that facilitates “mind speak.” (In lore surrounding creatures like Bigfoot, "mind-speak" describes the reported phenomenon where witnesses feel they receive thoughts, concepts, or emotions directly rather than hearing an audible voice.)

“My experience as a child with the Sasquatch. I fully believe that when I heard, ‘Don’t fall. Don’t fall’ as I raced home was the first benevolent support from the consciously connected Sabe. I have been able to, with permission, be allowed to shape shift into a connected Sabe. I use a connecting action that allows me to view through Sabe’s experience. This connection opens a “portal” that either opens to their physical form or just remains a remote aerial view.”

She has tried to remain silent about this “gifted” ability, but circumstances have exposed this. “I was always afraid that it would lead to being an experiment. But teaching others is not what Sabe intends currently. She wonders, “Could this be the opening up to connecting our consciousness in greater numbers? I can’t predict, but it is what is needed to move forward for the environment and ultimately their survival?”

From a post-conference email, “Bill, my exposure is in your hands, and Sabe knows.”

Migration patterns

Then a citizen science perspective. Josh Meecha presented an overview of migration patterns at the conference.

“I'm from all the way out in LA (Los Angeles), and I've been interested for about 20 years off and on. Initially due to all the stories out of Yosemite. Then I got interested as part of the cryptozoology branch of science.

“For me, researching Sasquatch has always felt like a childhood hunt for buried gold—except the treasure isn’t a chest in the dirt; it’s the truth hidden across decades of scattered evidence. My passion lies in moving past folklore to build a solid, corroborated case for the species' existence. By leveraging AI to synthesize thousands of historical sightings, track findings, and environmental data points, I can cross-reference patterns at a scale that transforms isolated stories into a cohesive ecological map.

Animals move or migrate, so do Sasquatch. He explained the migration data shows that these movements don't happen in a vacuum: “They closely mirror the established migration corridors and seasonal patterns of Ontario’s largest known wildlife, particularly moose, white-tailed deer, and black bears. Whether shadowing ungulate herds directly or relying on the same path-of-least-resistance terrain, caloric bottlenecks, and sheltered winter yards, Sasquatch sightings consistently map onto known big-game trajectories.”

Josh explained, “When you overlay these wildlife corridors across Ontario, North Bay emerges as the ultimate geographic and ecological hub - the North–South Axis. North Bay sits right on the biological transition line between the boreal forest and Great Lakes–St. Lawrence ecosystems. This corridor links the vast, undisturbed wilderness of Temagami and the James Bay lowlands in the north directly to the hardwood ridges and deep valleys of the Algonquin Dome to the south—following the exact routes large ungulates and predators use to shift between dense winter conifer cover and summer foraging grounds.

“The East–West Axis: Anchored by Lake Nipissing, the Trout Lake chain, and the ancient Mattawa–French River waterway, this natural riparian highway funnels large wildlife movement between the Ottawa Valley and Quebec timberlands in the east and the rugged Canadian Shield stretching toward Georgian Bay and Algoma in the west.”

He said, “By treating these sightings as biological data moving in lockstep with known megafauna rather than isolated myth, we begin to see an elusive apex species navigating Ontario’s oldest natural crossroads.”

Be on the lookout and get a road map; maybe the paper one is still in the glove box (that’s history…maps and glove boxes).

Ontario Sasquatch

Peter Smith was at the conference, and he is the founder of Ontario Sasquatch. (There is a big difference between the two sites - Sasquatch Ontario, see Mike Patterson below – Others.)

Peter said, “I was pleased to see so many Indigenous people there. It took years to gain their trust. Now, about half our members are Indigenous. Christine (Brynes), being an Elder/Grandmother, has helped a lot.”

As I was writing this, he shared/sent some recent reports.

There are apparently three white Sasquatch reports. “What is significant about this one is that it was at Trout Creek, on Hwy 522…near Grundy Lake Provincial Park is the report that I talked about in my presentation, that has had activity for over 20 years, and two of our investigators saw a white Sabé in November 2022. We think it may be the same Sabé, 13 years later, and 100 km west.”

This also reminded me of the rare white moose sightings near Foleyet.

There’s a Bigfoot reporting hotline, 647-508-2400, and they are taking applications for investigators (in existence since 2018).

Others

A couple of other well-known, within the realm of this community, Sasquatch aficionados, who did not attend this conference.

Tim Ervick (Timothy D online. “Douglas is my middle name.”) is the founder of Ontario Bigfoot, and there are Temagami examples on the site with a being called “Old Yellow Top.”

He’s been involved in Bigfoot research for more than 20 years. “

“It started with curiosity about the subject and grew through some unusual experiences while spending time in the northern Ontario wilderness. Eventually, I decided to take a more serious approach to investigating reports and documenting what people were experiencing.

“Ontario Bigfoot focuses primarily on field investigations, eyewitness reports, and gathering evidence. I'm a firm believer that Bigfoot is a flesh-and-blood creature, but I also believe claims need to be backed up by evidence.”

Another expert.

Mike Paterson of Sasquatch Ontario (not Ontario Sasquatch) has 191 videos, with more than ten million views. He has reportedly had contact with a Sasquatch family since 2012.

“What I'm involved in is far removed from what most are involved with. Hundreds of encounter incidents that continue to show me who they are and give insight into this enduring mystery.

He said, “Many have a difficult time accepting my supporting evidence and that is because it's as I just mentioned, it's far beyond the "norm". I had an experience in 2008 that showed me their existence. I wanted answers, and I've spent now 18 years getting those answers, and then some.

One of his projects was a vocal comparison video. “Because of a video I found on YouTube, there were some campers who were hearing a Sasquatch vocalize not far from them. That Sasquatch sounded just like Nef, one of whom I interact with. Two similar vocal tones, two different countries. I've accumulated an extensive database of their vocals and sounds over the years.” He is now 18 years involved in this subject, fourteen of those years involving ongoing contact with the same family.

As for what people think of his longitudinal study.

“Comments tend to be supportive, although that's taken many years for people to learn to accept what I'm sharing is authentic. Still understandably difficult for many, and there are always trolls. I don't hold back much; I speak a truth that shatters our current paradigm. Sasquatch are ancient people who hold abilities that have allowed them to hold onto that mythical status and keep humans guessing or denying. I've stood firm in my experience and knowledge and have watched this subject unfold, stating similar things from others as the years pass.”

Mike will be on the Back Roads Bill podcast, Wed., December 2 (“Looking forward to it, said Back Roads Bill).

Mike says, “I've done many interviews over the years. I'm comfortable sharing my experiences, so no problem if you want to do a podcast. I prefer questions on the spot, so I don't need them beforehand. It's more authentic that way. I know my stuff Bill. I don't hold back for most part. If you're ready to hear the truth and step outside this 3D realm, I'm well versed in my understanding of Sasquatch and who they are.”

He has learned through firsthand experience that Sasquatch truth shatters our current paradigm, a shift in consciousness through contact from ancient people who, at this time in our history, are reaching out to those they choose, helping us see the infinite multiverse beyond our limited perception.

“Sasquatch truth is mystery and magic that exposes an infinite world of understanding for those open-minded to experiencing truth and reality as it is meant to be. Sasquatch contact gives hope for the human race.” His book ‘Invisible Giant’ was released earlier this year.

He wasn't invited to the North Bay gathering. “I will, however, be giving a presentation up in Thunder Bay next weekend (October 17th) at the Paracon Event.

This event sounded interesting and was at a wonderful heritage venue.

On the website, “Start the weekend with dinner alongside Paracon guest speakers before heading into Fort William Historical Park's buildings after dark... and experience what happens when the Fort gets quiet....” I have been there a few times; I think it is a perfect venue for such a conference at night!

“Hear incredible stories from paranormal investigators, psychic mediums, authors, occult experts, Sasquatch researchers and experiencers from across Canada and the U.S.”

“A full day exploring the unexplained - for just $66.”

(Hmm…I’m in the next time!)

There were many cryptid colourful shirts in attendance. One was AshleyNicole (sic) Brooker, who said, “I had a great time at my first Bigfoot conference. I met some great people, heard some wonderful stories and felt right at home with everyone.”

“I believe I have always been connected to nature. But it wasn't until a few years ago. I did some research. There were visions and dreams of reassurance. And found myself with an encounter with Bigfoot... but what I have seen, felt, and experienced... it has made me a huge believer!”

For AshleyNicole, “The Bigfoot conference was not only about people who have had encounters or experiences in the field. It was a huge comforting moment for me …knowing what I know and sharing it, that no one will understand until it happens to them.”

And BRB will take her up on her offer. “I remember you loved the shirt I was wearing, so I'm going to make you one for the next time I see you or at the next conference.” (See Oct. 15-17, 2027).

By the time I finished this story, I went ahead and created a survey. You can participate; go here; there are only two questions, it will take seconds; I will give an update with the New Year’s look back on all the BRB stories. Now, read on for the conference’s audience results.

Finally

My Thanksgiving presentation was a summary of how the media has addressed cryptids over decades. It was a chronological look at how Sasquatch and the like have been perceived.

I cited the early, most famous black-and-white, grainy footage from Frame 352 of what launched the phenomenon, the Roger Patterson and Robert Gimlin 1967 clip, which depicts an unidentified subject the filmmakers asserted was Bigfoot on the back roads of northern California.

And then movies like Pottersville (2017) and Harry and the Hendersons (1987). There was a gradual societal change in the perception/representation of the cryptids.

For the audience, I said, “For me Sasquatch symbolizes wilderness areas on the back waters and back roads - vast, like northern Ontario – always inviting. For those who love the outdoors, Sasquatch legends serve as reminders of nature’s unpredictability and the endless possibilities it holds.

“Whether or not Sasquatch exists, the pursuit of its legend encourages people to adventure into the wild, fostering a deeper connection with the natural world.”

Here is an Ontario Parks blog that complements my thinking (Park Naturalist Roger LaFontaine, a classically trained biologist and amateur Sasquatch researcher). He says, “Our parks aren’t just for human recreation; they also maintain the ecological integrity of our landscape. Next time you head out on a camping or hiking trip, just remember: you might be sharing the landscape with Sasquatch.”

That day, and it was an intriguing one, my favourite question from the audience was to conference organizer Andrew Mackellar and Father Jim, who were explaining how peanut butter jars are left out in the middle of winter in Sasquatch-prone areas and how evidence points to their manual manipulation.

The audience participant asked, “Do they like smooth or crunchy?

Without missing a beat, Andrew said, “Good question, we will have to change it up in our field research and find out.” (You can see BRB in costume on the podcast.)

Back to that conference cryptid question about “flesh and blood,” or “related to the paranormal?”

By far, from the straw dog hand count, it was surprisingly related to the paranormal circa seventy-five percent. You’ve done the survey.

If you relate to “social residue” or “social fields,” there was a great deal of energy in that hall, that Sasquatch Saturday.

Next year’s event is called the ‘Northern Ontario Sasquatch Festival'–a weekend affair (October 15-17, 2027) – at the Canadian Ecology Centre – home of Sasquatch Sam.

Of course I am asked. I always cite the endearing primate scientist, Jane Goodall (with a well-established link to Sudbury’s regreening project), who passed last year, who said, “Well, I'm a romantic, so I always wanted them to exist.”

Back roads, especially in wilderness areas, are ripe for cryptid legends, local folklore, and unexplained encounters.

That’s why I frequent them.
